note: THE EVOLVABILITY FIXTURE (kogaki#654 acceptance item 6, story 1.91).
A workflow table that is NOT the shipped one, exercised by
checks/check-terrain-workflow.sh to make #625's evolvability claim
CHECKABLE rather than asserted. The claim is that order, kinds, waits,
conditionality and stopping are read from the table on every run and are
held nowhere in the executor — so a table that differs in exactly those
dimensions must run correctly with ZERO changes to executor control code.
IT DIFFERS IN BOTH DIMENSIONS THE ACCEPTANCE ITEM NAMES:
- A MOVED HANDOFF. The shipped table's first wait sits third, after a
compute and a write. Here the first wait is FIRST — the run stops
before it has computed anything. If any stopping behaviour were
positional rather than table-read, this is where it would show.
- AN ADDED ENTRY POINT. `reconsider` is a state the shipped table does
not have, and `second_thoughts` is a second conditional wait. Neither
id appears in the executor.
SEAM-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is a design constraint rather than a
convenience: every state here is `compute`, `wait` or `terminal`, the
three kinds KIND_SEMANTICS marks as needing no renderer. A `write` state
would need a renderer bound to its id, every shipped renderer composes
from a survey, and a survey needs the seam — so a fixture table carrying
a write state could not be driven without the substrate. THE LIMIT IS
STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this fixture exercises order, waits,
conditionality, resumption and stopping, and does NOT exercise
owner-artifact writing. The shipped-table block of the same check is what
covers the write count, against the real table.
`counted_baseline` is this table's OWN declaration and disagrees with the
shipped one deliberately — the check counts each table against itself,
which is the property acceptance item 6 asks for.

governing_text: specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §15.1 — a new state is a table row PLUS a renderer, and the executor interprets the table and invents neither

state_kinds.compute: no owner surface, no renderer needed
state_kinds.wait: the executor stops; the owner speaks; re-enter with --input
state_kinds.terminal: the end of a run, read from the table and never from position

states.owner_supplies: what they are looking for, in free text
states.note: THE MOVED HANDOFF. In the shipped table the first wait is the third state; here it is the first, so the run stops before computing anything.
stands in for the shipped table's survey — same kind, no renderer, no seam.
THE ADDED ENTRY POINT. No such id exists in the shipped table or in the executor.

states.conditional: entered only with --enter second_thoughts; never scheduled by the flow

counted_baseline_note: Declared by hand and compared against the baseline the executor DERIVES from the states array above. The check refuses on a disagreement; that refusal is the fixture's whole point, so a mutation of either number is its efficacy case.
